subject: economics
keySource: NTA CUET (UG) 2026 final key rows matched by question id (ids/cuet2026-economics-keyrows.json); 50 of 50 authenticated
bankRead: saved read-only snapshot of 20 Nov 2026 (scratchpad econA/bank_economics.json 410 visible rows, served_economics.json 238 served ids, suspended.json); no database access

method: tmp/1120-speed/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; passage-printed answers are skill; numericals need a served bank item with the same formula and steps)

figure.note: covered over counted (covered + not covered); skill, off-syllabus and dropped are shown, not counted

facts: all combinations producible from given resources and technology = production possibility set
questions.reason: Key card gives the question's own definition and names it the production possibility set.

facts: optimum is where the budget line is tangent to an indifference curve (A)
the consumer seeks the highest indifference curve within the budget set, so D (on the budget line, lower curve) is inferior
B and C lie outside the budget set

matches.teaches: move to the highest possible indifference curve given the budget set
interior optimum where MRS = price ratio

questions.reason: Cards teach the tangency optimum and that the consumer moves to the highest curve she can afford, so the affordable point on a lower curve is the inferior one.

facts: eD = % change in quantity / % change in price = 50% / 50% = 1

matches.teaches: definition only (card, does not cover a numerical)
meaning of elastic demand, no computation

questions.reason: No served bank question computes a price elasticity from two prices and two quantities.

facts: q = f(y1, y2) is the production function
f(ty) = t.f(y): CRS
f(ty) > t.f(y): IRS
f(ty) < t.f(y): DRS

matches.teaches: A: q = f(L, K) production function
C and D: IRS and DRS formulas

questions.reason: All four pairs are on Key cards in the same notation.

facts: isoquants are negatively sloped (so "positively sloped" is not a characteristic)
isoquant = input combinations giving the same maximum output, labelled with that output
questions.reason: No served item or card mentions isoquants at all.

facts: one variable input increased with others fixed
TP first rises at an increasing rate
then at a diminishing rate
after its maximum TP declines

matches.teaches: B: vary one input, keep others constant
MP first rises then falls (not the TP stages)
MP of the variable input eventually declines

questions.reason: Material teaches the MP shape, but the three TP stages (increasing rate, diminishing rate, decline after the maximum) are stated nowhere.

questions.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
facts: short-run profit max at positive output: p = SMC, SMC non-decreasing, p >= AVC
p < SAC is not a condition
questions.reason: Key card lists exactly the three keyed conditions, which leaves out statement A.

questions.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
facts: a rise in an input price (wage) shifts the MC curve upward (leftward)

matches.teaches: leftward (or upward) shift of the MC curve
MC = wage / MP, so MC moves with the wage

questions.reason: Key card says a rise in an input price makes an upward shift of the MC curve.

facts: in perfect competition the Invisible Hand changes price when the market is out of balance

matches.teaches: raises price in excess demand, lowers in excess supply

questions.reason: Key card states the Invisible Hand changes price whenever there is imbalance.

facts: a price ceiling is set below the equilibrium price
it creates excess demand
rationing through fair price shops can lead to a black market

matches.teaches: ceiling below equilibrium leads to excess demand
kerosene named as a ceiling item
ceiling below equilibrium causes a shortage

questions.reason: Cards and a served bank item teach that the ceiling sits below equilibrium, so "above" is the false statement; the other three are taught.

facts: Keynes's General Theory was published in 1936

matches.teaches: names The General Theory, no year

questions.reason: The book is named on a card, but its 1936 publication year appears nowhere (macro chapter 1 is mapped to National Income).

facts: transactions of the domestic economy with the rest of the world = the external sector

matches.teaches: BoP records transactions with the rest of the world (not the sector name)

questions.reason: The term "external sector" is taught by no served item or card.

facts: the RBI regulates the money supply (sterilisation is the RBI's, as the monetary authority)

matches.teaches: RBI uses CRR to regulate money supply

questions.reason: Material teaches the RBI regulates money supply, which settles the authority; the word sterilisation itself is not taught (flagged for B).

facts: M1 = CU + DD
M2 = M1 + post office savings deposits
M3 = M1 + net time deposits of commercial banks
M4 = M3 + total post office deposits excluding NSC
questions.reason: Each of the four definitions is a Key card in the same words.

facts: money multiplier = 1 / reserve ratio = 1 / 0.5 = 2
questions.reason: A served bank question computes the multiplier as 1 over the reserve ratio, the same formula, steps and unknown.

facts: buying and selling government securities by the central bank = open market operations

matches.teaches: buying raises, selling cuts money supply

questions.reason: Key cards define OMO and its effect on money supply.

facts: rate of increase in ex ante consumption per unit increment in income = MPC

matches.teaches: MPC = change in C / change in Y

questions.reason: Key card is the question's sentence word for word.

facts: (A) ex ante = planned: true
(B) ex post = actual: true
(C) keyed false: "consumption changes at a constant rate the changes in income"
(D) consumption function relates consumption and income: true

matches.teaches: C = C-bar + cY (a constant c, which reads as making C true)

questions.reason: A, B and D are taught, but nothing teaches why statement C is false; the served C = C-bar + cY card would lead a student to accept it.

matches.teaches: reads C-bar and c from C = 100 + 0.8Y (card, does not cover a numerical)
multiplier on a change, not the equilibrium level

questions.reason: No served bank question solves for equilibrium income from a consumption function and investment.

facts: a change in autonomous spending changes output by a larger amount through the multiplier
questions.reason: Key card is the question's sentence with the multiplier named.

facts: equilibrium output below full-employment output = deficient demand

matches.teaches: excess demand is the opposite case

questions.reason: Key card names this situation deficient demand.

facts: investment multiplier = 1 / (1 - MPC)
questions.reason: A served bank explanation states the multiplier as 1/(1 - MPC).

facts: budget functions are allocation, redistribution and stabilisation; consumption is not one
questions.reason: Key card lists the three functions, which excludes consumption.

facts: (A) public goods are consumed collectively (benefits available to all)
(B) may be produced by government or private sector
(C) non-rivalrous
(D) non-excludable

matches.teaches: A: benefits available to all, not restricted to one consumer
B: may be produced by the government or the private sector, verbatim

questions.reason: All four features are on Key cards; B is word for word.

facts: change in Y = change in G x 1/(1 - c) = 100 x 5 = 500

matches.teaches: MPC 0.6, G rises by 100: multiplier 2.5, change in Y = 250

questions.reason: A served bank question computes the change in income from a rise in G with the simple multiplier, the same formula and steps.

facts: automatic stabiliser: income tax
revenue payment (expenditure): neither creates an asset nor reduces a liability
capital receipt: creates a liability or reduces an asset
total expenditure: plan and non-plan

matches.teaches: A: proportional income tax is an automatic stabiliser
B: revenue expenditure neither creates assets nor reduces liabilities
D: plan and non-plan capital expenditure

questions.reason: A, B and C are stated outright; cards split both revenue and capital expenditure into plan and non-plan for D.

facts: imports rise: demand for foreign goods rises
demand curve for foreign exchange shifts right
exchange rate (price of foreign currency) rises
that rise is depreciation of the domestic currency

matches.teaches: imports up: demand curve shifts right, depreciation
rise in price of foreign currency = depreciation

questions.reason: Cards give the chain from more imports to a rightward shift to depreciation, which is the name for the rise in the rate.

facts: market-determined rate with central bank intervention = managed floating

matches.teaches: central banks intervene to moderate movements

questions.reason: Key cards describe managed floating in these terms.

facts: imports are a leakage, exports an injection
questions.reason: Two Key cards state both halves.

facts: current account deficit: receipts < payments

matches.teaches: BoP (not current account) deficit when autonomous receipts < payments
trade (goods) deficit when imports exceed exports

questions.reason: Near miss: cards give the current account balance condition and the BoP deficit, but never state the current account deficit direction.

questions.chapter: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
facts: first census of British India: 1881
questions.reason: Key card gives 1881.

facts: Planning Commission 1950
Second Five Year Plan after the first plan 1951-56 (IPR 1956 its basis)
Green Revolution from the mid-1960s
New Economic Policy 1991

matches.teaches: B: IPR 1956 the basis of the Second Plan

questions.reason: Cards date all four events, which fixes the order C, B, D, A.

facts: (A) industrial licensing abolished for all but a few categories
(B) private sector allowed in many industries (only atomic energy part and railway core reserved)
(C) many small-scale goods dereserved
(D) price controls were a pre-reform regulation, not a reform

matches.teaches: A: licensing kept only for a short list
A: licensing deregulated for most industries
D: price controls listed as a pre-1991 regulation

questions.reason: A, B and D are taught; the dereservation of small-scale goods (C) is stated by no served item or card.

facts: outsourcing: hiring regular service from external sources
stabilisation: correct BoP weaknesses and inflation
structural: efficiency and international competitiveness
globalisation: integration with the world economy

matches.teaches: D: globalisation = integration with world economy

questions.reason: All four pairs are Key card definitions.

facts: Kothari Commission 1964-66
Tapas Majumdar Committee 1999
RTE Act 2009
National Education Policy 2020

matches.teaches: only the Directive Principles (none of the four)

questions.reason: None of the four education milestones or their years is taught.

facts: environment supplies renewable and non-renewable resources, assimilates waste, sustains life (genetic and biodiversity), gives aesthetic services
questions.reason: Key card lists the four functions in the question's words.

facts: Union Ministry of Labour collects formal sector employment data
construction workers: casual wage labourers
MGNREGA: rural employment
TANWA: women workers

matches.teaches: B: construction workers as casual wage labourers

questions.reason: Two of four pairs taught; the Labour Ministry's data role and TANWA are taught nowhere.

facts: China followed the classical pattern: agriculture to manufacturing to services
questions.reason: Key card names China and the classical pattern.

facts: Pakistan announced its first five year plan in 1956
questions.reason: Key card gives 1956 for Pakistan.

questions.reason: Card gives the China, India, Pakistan order; every option puts USA first, so that part is not tested.

facts: three methods: product (value added), income, expenditure

matches.teaches: three methods give the same estimate

questions.reason: Key card names the three methods; the passage does not.

questions.reason: No served bank question computes real GDP at base-year prices.

matches.teaches: formula only (card, does not cover a numerical)

facts: domestic services women perform at home are non-monetary exchanges

matches.teaches: this exact example under non-monetary exchanges

questions.reason: Key card gives the domestic-services example under non-monetary exchanges; the passage names the category but not the example.

facts: the passage states CPI and WPI are the other important ways to measure price change
questions.reason: The keyed sentence is printed in the GDP and Welfare passage; it tests reading, not stored material (METHOD decision).

facts: rural development = action for the development of (rural) areas lagging behind in socio-economic development

matches.teaches: action for areas lagging behind in the development of the village economy

questions.reason: Key card defines rural development as action for lagging areas of the village economy, which picks the rural-areas option.

facts: the passage names organic farming as an eco-friendly technology
questions.reason: The answer is printed in the Rural Development passage; it tests reading (METHOD decision).

facts: the passage says group savings are channelled through micro credit which functions like mini banks
questions.reason: The answer is printed in the Rural Development passage; it tests reading (METHOD decision). A card also teaches micro-credit programmes.

facts: diversification: change in cropping pattern and shift of workforce to allied activities and non-agriculture
questions.reason: Key card gives the two aspects of diversification in the question's words; the passage only uses the word.

facts: marketing policy instruments: MSP, buffer stocks, PDS; private trade is not one
questions.reason: Key card lists the three instruments, leaving private trade out.
